The dogfood byte-identity suite emits ONE assertion per generator-owned file, so its count tracks how many files the generator owns. This work retired canonical templates -- delivery-blueprint-template.md with BLUEPRINT.md, and delivery-plans/flattened-plan-template.md with the Lite path's PLAN.md -- so there is one fewer file to compare per tree and the count drops accordingly. Nothing stopped being CHECKED: every file that still exists is still compared in both directions, and the suite's own ORPHAN and MUT-CTRL legs (which assert there are no undocumented extra files, and that the comparison can still detect a mutation) both pass. A reduction here is the expected arithmetic of deleting a template, not lost coverage -- which is why it belongs in this file rather than in a re-home: there is no new key to point at.
